summary:
M1a is almost entirely greenfield. Verified against the code: only purge-model (Target with 9 string-path variants, Band/Tool/ScanMode/Category, Plan `purge.plan/0`), the purge-engine argument parser (bins/purge-engine/src/main.rs, every verb prints "not implemented") and tools/xtask (ui-strings, check-deps, ci) contain real code; all other crates are doc-comment stubs. kb/*.json are empty arrays; kb/baselines has EnterpriseSEval-26100.1742 and Professional-26340.9882. .cargo/config.toml already sets +crt-static, so the engine exe runs in the guest without a redistributable. No unins*.dat or .lnk fixture exists in the repo (absent).

Design: 25 packages in 6 waves. Wave 0 fixes every shared file once (all Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, every lib.rs mod list, empty module stubs) and lands the §5.2 model, so later packages only fill in their own module files and never touch a manifest or lib.rs. Wave 1 is the pure/leaf layer (guard, policy, Inno parser, tokenizer, baseline+matcher, source traits+Fixture, purge-win FFI). Wave 2 is inventory, runner, live source, targeted index queries, identity assembly, scan framework, decide+plan. Wave 3 is harvest (two packages), the 17 scanners (four packages) and rig glue (two packages). Wave 4 wires the CLI; wave 5 adds offline replay + scanner-coverage. The gate then runs in the VM.

Three design choices worth knowing:
1. Fixture can load a rig snap (`snap-*.tsv.gz` + `lists-*.json`) directly, so the whole pipeline can be replayed offline: harvest on snap1, scan on snap2, score with rigtool. This gives a fast loop without the VM. Limits: no file contents, no REG_BINARY data, previews cut at 1024 chars.
2. Engine runs in the VM must use a run name different from the app id (e.g. `r0-vscode`), because vm/rig.ps1 `Move-RunToOld` would otherwise archive the frozen M0 run directories that vm/truth/recompute.sh reads.
3. The M1a scanner list cannot meet two M1a exit criteria on its own. Notepad++ frozen truth is 29 items, of which only `HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Notepad++` is reachable by M1a scanners: 1/29 = 3.4 %, exactly BCU's number, so "better than BCU" fails without an `AppxPackage` offer. §1.4 also asks for "Sparse AppX package Likely" for VS Code and Notepad++. SYS-APPX is listed under M1b. The breakdown therefore includes a minimal read-only sparse-package link (marked APPX-MIN in P12/P15/P30/P32); it needs your confirmation (see questions).

Expected M1a recall ceilings from frozen truth (vm/truth/frozen): Git 2/16 (the two Classes keys; the rest is Prefetch, jump lists, UserAssist, JumplistData, UFH, temp, all M1b/M4/v2), Firefox roughly 8-9/24 (BCU 20.8 %), VS Code about 135+/154 through skeletons on the LTSC baseline (BCU 0 %), Notepad++ about 22+/29 only with the package offer.

Importance routing used: engine correctness/safety logic critical; FFI, CLI, runner, live plumbing high; rig glue medium; scaffolding trivial.

packages.title: Inno Setup uninstall-log parser (unins*.dat)
crates_files: crates/purge-harvest/src/inno.rs and private submodules under crates/purge-harvest/src/inno/
crates/purge-harvest/tests/fixtures/inno/** (synthetic logs built by a test helper; real logs added at the gate)
packages.scope: Pure byte parser written from the public issrc `Setup.UninstallLog.pas` format (attribution line in the header comment; nothing from draft_clone). 448-byte header: ID string, AppId, AppName, Version, NumRecs, EndOffset, Flags, reserved, CRC32 over the header; version gate: parse versions <= 1055, otherwise return `Unsupported{version}` so the caller records a warning and falls back to harvest-only. Body: blocks of up to 4096 bytes each prefixed `{Size u32, NotSize u32, CRC u32}` with NotSize == !Size and CRC checked; concatenated stream of records `{Typ u16, ExtraData u32, DataSize u32}` followed by DataSize bytes of packed strings: length marker byte 0x00-0xFC literal length, 0xFD u16 length, 0xFE i32 length (negative = UTF-16LE byte count), 0xFF end. Record types 0x80-0x8B decoded into typed records: Run, DeleteDirOrFiles, DeleteFile, DeleteGroupOrItem, IniDeleteEntry, IniDeleteSection, RegDeleteEntireKey, RegClearValue, RegDeleteKeyIfEmpty, RegDeleteValue, DecrementSharedCount, RefreshFileAssoc, MutexCheck (unknown types kept as Raw with a warning, never an error). Flags surfaced: 64-bit view (`ExtraData & 0x01000000`), ExistedBeforeInstall, SharedFile, RegisteredServer and the per-type flag bits. Output maps to model `InnoRecord`s: registry root constants to canonical hives (HKCU records keep a `user` marker for the caller to bind to a SID), view, path, value name; file paths as written. All lengths bounds-checked; malformed input returns an error, never panics; cap total decoded size (e.g. 64 MiB).
packages.acceptance: A synthetic writer in the test module produces logs for versions at and below the gate; parse(write(x)) == x. Corrupt CRC, truncated block, NotSize mismatch, oversized length, version > 1055 each produce the specific error/Unsupported value. When a real Git or VS Code unins000.dat is supplied via env `PURGE_INNO_FIXTURES` (directory), the ignored test parses it fully with zero Raw records and prints record counts per type.
packages.tests: Unit tests on synthetic logs (ANSI and UTF-16 strings, all 12 types, 32/64-bit flags, multi-block records spanning a block boundary). A no-panic sweep: every single-byte truncation and 1,000 deterministic bit flips of a synthetic log return Ok or Err. `#[ignore]` test for real logs.

gate_procedure:
All commands from C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\uninstall\purge unless noted. Nothing here touches draft_clone or the commercial reference tool; installers come from official vendor URLs only (vm/guest/apps.ps1).

A. Local pre-gate (no VM)
1. `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, check-deps, ui-strings, scanner-coverage).
2. `cargo build --release -p purge-engine` -> target\release\purge-engine.exe (static CRT via .cargo/config.toml). `cargo build --release` in vm\rigtool; `cargo test` there.
3. Offline replay on the frozen M0 runs (needs the git-ignored vm\runs\{vscode,git,firefox,npp}): `cargo xtask replay-all`. This gives a first score against the exact frozen truth and BCU plans without a VM. It under-reports anything needing file contents (Inno log, shortcuts), so it is a development signal, not the gate.

B. VM runs (R0, post_uninstall) on the corpus VM Inbound-Win11-Test (EnterpriseSEval 26100.1742; matching baseline kb\baselines\EnterpriseSEval-26100.1742.tsv.gz)
4. `$env:VMPWFILE = '<password file>'; . .\vm\rig.ps1 -VmName Inbound-Win11-Test`
5. `Invoke-Campaign -Ids vscode,vscode-user,git,firefox,firefox-tb,npp -Nulls 0 -Snapshot rig-base -RunPrefix r0- -Engine .\target\release\purge-engine.exe` (parameters added by P36). Per run the rig restores rig-base, pushes rigtool.exe, purge-engine.exe, kb\baselines and the guest scripts, then in the guest: [pre-install Thunderbird for firefox-tb] -> lists0/snap0 -> install -> launch once at medium IL -> lists1/snap1 -> `purge-engine inventory --json > inv-1.json` -> `purge-engine harvest <program_id> -o fp.json` -> `purge-engine uninstall <program_id> --quiet --fp fp.json -o engine-run.json` -> settle -> lists2/snap2 -> `purge-engine scan --fp fp.json --mode post --app <truth id> -o plan-purge.json` -> `purge-engine inventory --json > inv-2.json` -> run.json. Outputs are pulled to vm\runs\r0-<id>\; the host copies plan-purge.json to vm\runs\r0-<id>\plans\purge.json. The frozen vm\runs\<id>\ directories are not touched because the run name differs from the app id.
6. Check each vm\runs\campaign-<stamp>.json row is ok and each run.json has uninstall.entry_gone = true and engine-run.json verify_gone.passed = true. A failed verify-gone means the plan was produced under forced rules and is not a valid R0.
7. Pull the real Inno logs once for parser fixtures (Git, VS Code system and user `unins000.dat` copied from the guest at the snap1 point by the run script into the run dir) and run the ignored parser test with PURGE_INNO_FIXTURES.

C. Truth for the new runs and scoring (from vm\, Git Bash) — `bash truth/m1a.sh` (P36), which does:
8. For each run r0-<id>: `rigtool/target/release/rigtool truth --s0 runs/r0-<id>/snap-r0-<id>-0.tsv.gz --s1 ...-1.tsv.gz --s2 ...-2.tsv.gz --lists0 runs/r0-<id>/lists-r0-<id>-0.json --lists2 ...-2.json --run runs/r0-<id>/run.json --ambient truth/ambient.json --labels truth/labels/<id>.json --deny truth/deny.json -o runs/r0-<id>/truth.json`. Labels: the frozen vscode/git/firefox/npp files; vscode-user.json and firefox-tb.json from P36.
9. Sanity against frozen truth: compare leftover/user_data counts and item lists of runs/r0-<id>/truth.json with truth/frozen/<id>/truth.json (expected: same items except random names such as temp files and jump-list hashes). Any other difference (for example something the engine's own uninstall command changed) is investigated before scoring; the frozen truth stays the reference for what counts as a leftover.
10. BCU on the same runs: copy truth/frozen/<id>/plans/bcu.json to runs/r0-<id>/plans/bcu.json for vscode, git, firefox, npp. For vscode-user and firefox-tb there is no BCU plan (see questions).
11. Score: `rigtool/target/release/rigtool score --set runs/r0-vscode runs/r0-vscode-user runs/r0-git runs/r0-firefox runs/r0-firefox-tb runs/r0-npp --deny truth/deny.json --json truth/m1a-score.json --md truth/m1a-score.md`.
12. Cross-check against the frozen sets as well: copy each purge.json into a scratch copy of the frozen set and run `rigtool score --plan <purge.json> --plan truth/frozen/<id>/plans/bcu.json --truth truth/frozen/<id>/truth.json --s0 runs/<id>/snap-<id>-0.tsv.gz --s2 runs/<id>/snap-<id>-2.tsv.gz --deny truth/deny.json --json ... --md ...` (items with run-specific random names score `gone`; used only to confirm danger 0 and precision on the frozen snapshots).

D. Pass criteria (read from truth/m1a-score.md, tool = purge, the `_nd` columns)
- danger_listed = 0 and danger_preselected = 0 on every run, including firefox-tb, where anything of Thunderbird's existed in snap0 and therefore scores danger.
- precision_safe = 100 % on every run; userdata_preselected = 0.
- recall_visible_nd(purge) > recall_visible_nd(bcu) per app: Firefox > 20.8 %, VS Code > 0 %, Git > 0 %, Notepad++ > 3.4 % (the last needs the AppxPackage offer).
- §1.4 bands, checked by hand from `purge-engine plan show` output and the score's hit/missed lists (the scorer does not check bands): VS Code system: OpenWithProgids values Safe, `.ext`/OpenWithProgids skeletons Safe (baseline matches on this VM), ApplicationAssociationToasts values Safe, PATH segment Safe if one is left, sparse package Likely. Git: `LibraryFolder\background\shell` and `sh_auto_file` Safe via ProvenOwnedSkeleton. Firefox: Mozilla\Firefox keys and Maintenance Service leftovers Safe, `ProgramData\Mozilla-<guid>\updates\<hash>` Safe, profiles (Roaming\Mozilla) Likely and not preselected, vendor parents delete-if-empty only, nothing of Thunderbird's listed in firefox-tb. Notepad++: no Notepad.lnk, sparse package Likely. Record the per-item band table in docs (an M1a report) with the plan hashes.
- Items §1.4 names that the vendor uninstaller already removed in these runs (Firefox ProgIDs, toast AUMID, Default Browser Agent task) are reported as 'not exercised', as FROZEN.md already notes.

E. Inventory criterion
13. For each run and phase 1 and 2: `rigtool invdiff --inv runs/r0-<id>/inv-<n>.json --lists runs/r0-<id>/lists-r0-<id>-<n>.json --explain truth/inventory-explain.json --json ... --md ...` must exit 0 (every difference explained).
